creator: Dan McCreary
subject: MicroSims

iframe
description: A p5.js infographic of the six layers behind a running MicroSim (iframe, HTML5, CSS, JavaScript, a JavaScript library and a CDN): click a layer for its role, code sample and dependencies, and press Break it to preview what the learner sees without it.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Web technologies that make up a MicroSim
learningObjectives: The learner will describe what HTML5, CSS, JavaScript, a JavaScript library, a CDN, and an iframe each contribute to a running MicroSim.

accessibility.notes: describe() summary; layer colors are always paired with text labels; hover dependencies are marked with a 'needed' tag as well as a gold outline

controls.label: Break it / Restore
controls.purpose: Remove the selected layer and preview the result, or put it back

controls.label: Six stack layers
controls.purpose: Select a layer to show its role, code sample, dependencies and failure mode

controls.label: Six stack layers
controls.purpose: Outline the layers the hovered layer depends on

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore-then-break: learners predict and observe the failure caused by removing each layer
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Clickable layered infographic with a failure preview
keyQuestions: What does the learner see if the CSS is missing?
Why do a missing library and an unreachable CDN look the same?
Which layer lets one MicroSim appear in many different pages?
commonMisconceptions: The iframe contains the MicroSim's code
CSS controls what the simulation does
A library loaded from a CDN works offline
assessmentOpportunities: Naming the missing layer from a described symptom
One-sentence descriptions of all six layers
